items.readable_text:
Content:
Trigonometric ratios can be used to solve for a missing side of a right triangle if one side is known along with the measure of an acute angle. However, the question of which ratio to use depends on what side is given and what side is unknown.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/e937c56bbecefecaf5de1b48673065ee]

Content:
In the triangle above, we are given an angle [MATH: \theta = 42^\circ,] and the length of the hypotenuse is given but the length of the side opposite is unknown.

Content:
So, we need to choose the trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite side to the hypotenuse. This is sine, and now we can just set up the ratio, as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \sin 42^{∘}|= (opposite)/(hypotenuse); = (x)/(8)]

Content:
Now, we simply solve for the unknown value [MATH: x,] as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \sin 42^{∘}|= (x)/(8); x|= 8\sin 42^{∘}; = 8(0.66913...); = 5.35304...; ≈ 5.4,]

Content:
rounded to the nearest tenth.

Content:
Note that we used a calculator to evaluate [MATH: \sin(42^\circ).]

sections.normalized_html:
For an angle [MATH: \theta] in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

  • [MATH: \sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}]

  • [MATH: \cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}]

  • [MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}]

First, notice that we are given the length of the leg [MATH: \overline{MO}] opposite the given angle [MATH: \angle{N}] and wish to find the length of the hypotenuse [MATH: \overline{NO}.]

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the hypotenuse is sine. Hence, [MATH: \sin (m∠N)|= (opposite leg)/(hypotenuse); \sin (32^{∘})|= (20)/(NO); NO ⋅ \sin (32^{∘})|= 20; NO|= (20)/(\sin (32^{∘})).]

Using a calculator to evaluate the trigonometric ratio, we conclude that [MATH: NO|= (20)/(\sin (32^{∘})); = (20)/((0.52991…)); = 37.74159…; ≈ 37.7,] rounded to one decimal place.

For an angle [MATH: \theta] in a right triangle, the trigonometric ratios are as follows:

- [MATH: \sin\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}]
- [MATH: \cos\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{adjacent leg}}{\textrm{hypotenuse}}]
- [MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{\textrm{opposite leg}}{\textrm{adjacent leg}}]

Notice that we are given the length of the leg [MATH: \overline{AB}] adjacent to the given angle [MATH: \angle A] and wish to find the length of the leg [MATH: \overline{BC}] opposite [MATH: \angle A.]

The trigonometric ratio that relates the opposite leg to the adjacent leg is tangent. Hence,
